title: IonQ Stock Tumbles on $2 Billion Equity Offering. Why Other Quantum Names Are Falling Just as Hard.
source_used: The Quantum Insider (IonQ press release); Investor's Business Daily excerpt
key_facts: IonQ priced a $2.0 billion equity offering
Offering is 20.5 million shares at $40.00 plus pre-funded warrants for 29.5 million shares at $40.00, about a 15% premium to the 13 Oct close
Also seven-year warrants for 100 million more shares at $69.46, a 100% premium to the 13 Oct close
Bought via underwriter J.P. Morgan by an entity managed by Heights Capital Management
CEO Niccolo de Masi called IonQ the best-capitalized pure-play quantum company
IBD: IonQ stock fell Wednesday; the offering follows the Elisity all-stock deal that dilutes existing holders
Headlines (Yahoo Finance): IonQ fell about 6%, D-Wave and Rigetti about 4%
quote_evidence: The offering consists of 20,500,000 shares of IonQ’s common stock, each at $40.00 per share
IonQ (IONQ) stock fell on Wednesday after the quantum computing company announced a $2 billion equity offering
why_it_matters_hint: New shares and warrants can dilute current holders, which is why the stock and its peers fell.
notes: Barron's blocked (401). Offering terms from IonQ's own release as carried by The Quantum Insider; stock fall from IBD text; the 6% / 4% figures are from a Yahoo Finance headline only.
